ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the top side of the large rectangle WXYZ is WX, and the right side is XY. The large rectangle is divided into upper and lower two layers, with a total of seven congruent small rectangles: the upper layer has 4 vertically placed small rectangles side by side filling the width, and the lower layer has 3 horizontally placed small rectangles side by side filling the same width. Then reason: Let the short side of each small rectangle be s, and the long side be l. The width of each vertically placed rectangle in the upper layer is s, so the width of the large rectangle WX = 4s; the width of each horizontally placed rectangle in the lower layer is l, so the same width WX = 3l. Therefore 4s = 3l, obtaining l = 4s/3. The height XY of the large rectangle equals the upper-layer height plus the lower-layer height, namely l + s = 4s/3 + s = 7s/3. Thus WX:XY = 4s : 7s/3 = 12:7.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as two horizontal layers inside rectangle WXYZ: the top layer contains 4 congruent small rectangles placed upright, and the bottom layer contains 3 congruent small rectangles placed sideways. Let the short side of each small rectangle be s and the long side be l. From the top layer, the total width WX is 4s and the top-layer height is l. From the bottom layer, the same total width WX is 3l and the bottom-layer height is s. Equate the common width: 4s = 3l, so l = 4s/3. Then the large rectangle height XY is l + s = 4s/3 + s = 7s/3, while WX = 4s. Therefore WX:XY = 4s : 7s/3 = 12:7.
